title: Finite reduction of purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$1\leq m\leq n$, and write $\operatorname{red}_{n,m,T}$ for the finite
reduction functor

$$
K\mapsto K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}:\
D^b_{ctf}(T,A_{E,n})\longrightarrow D^b_{ctf}(T,A_{E,m})
$$

on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$. For a smooth separated
morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, of pure
relative dimension $d$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$, the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}\operatorname{red}_{n,m,X}\bigl(Lf^*K(d)[2d]\bigr)
& \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{red}_{n,m}(\gamma_{f,K})\ }& \operatorname{red}_{n,m,X}(Rf^!K)\\
\big\downarrow\ \sim
& & \big\downarrow\ \sim\\
Lf^*\operatorname{red}_{n,m,Y}K(d)[2d]
& \xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{f,\operatorname{red}_{n,m}K}\ }& Rf^!_{A_{E,m}}\operatorname{red}_{n,m,Y}K
\end{array}$$

commutes, the vertical isomorphisms being the finite-reduction
compatibilities of the six-operations package. The same is true for the
affine orientations of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation], the smooth
traces of [def-pur-smooth-trace], the composition coherence of
[thm-pur-composition-coherence], and the base-change squares of
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence].

proof.text: Step 1 (domains and twists). Write $A=A_{E,n}$, $B=A_{E,m}$ and $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. These are positive finite stages, on the finite-type schemes required by [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. If $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, [lem-sf-flat-model] and [lem-sf-reduction-flat-model] give a flat model of $Q_TK$ in the same interval. The finite-reduction assertion of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] supplies the bounded constructible comparisons for pullback, tensor and compact supports on these finite-Tor domains. Use [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] with its larger index equal to our $n$ and smaller index equal to our $m$ to obtain $Q_XRf_n^!K\cong Rf_m^!Q_YK$, with the unit, counit and quotient-cocycle compatibilities. No flatness of $A\to B$ is asserted. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], $A_T(1)$ is a locally free rank-one sheaf and is the specified reduction of the integral line. Tensor associativity gives $A_T(1)\otimes_A B=B_T(1)$. Tensor powers give this identity for positive twists; the zero twist is $A_T$, and for negative twists the dual of a rank-one free module reduces to its dual (locally, both maps are $\operatorname{Hom}_A(A,A)\otimes_A B=B$). Thus the definition in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] gives $Q_T(K(r))\cong (Q_TK)(r)$ for every integer $r$. Derived tensor commutes with shifts, giving the left vertical comparison in the square; the exceptional comparison gives the right vertical one.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: operation comparisons and finite-Tor boundedness

proof.text: Step 2 (the tensor map and structural comparisons). Put $\omega_{f,A}=Rf_n^!A_Y$. The tensor transformation of [def-pur-co-smoothness] is the adjoint of the compact-support projection-formula inverse followed by the coefficient-object counit. The projection transformation is [def-exchange-projection]; [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] makes it invertible on these finite-level etale-origin objects, and [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] makes its tensor mate an isomorphism. Apply [lem-pur-finite-adjoint-mate-compatibility] with the quotient $A\to B$: it identifies this tensor map, adjoint transposition of supported maps, the exceptional composition comparison, and the extraordinary base-change comparison with their $B$-versions. Its hypotheses are the pullback/tensor/compact-support comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], the unit/counit comparison of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], and the canonical extraordinary comparison [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary], whose etale mate is specified in [prop-asd-smooth-base-change]. Thus all structural identifications used below reduce independently of an orientation.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: tensor formula and exceptional-adjunction coefficient comparison; adjunction formulas written out

proof.text: Step 3 (the affine orientation at all finite levels). Apply [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] to the zero divisor $s:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$. Its supported map $c_{s(Y),A}:s_*A_Y\to A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ is the supported Kummer boundary and commutes with every quotient $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$, without a divisibility condition on either index. Its adjoint is the orientation $A_Y\to Rs^!A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ characterized in [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. Apply the mate formula of Step 2 to this supported map, using [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] for $s$; the reduced adjoint is precisely the adjoint of $c_{s(Y),B}$. This proves the affine-orientation assertion. In particular no assertion about tensoring cohomology groups with a nonflat quotient is needed. Products of these orientations reduce to the corresponding products because tensor and its associativity comparisons are preserved by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; this also preserves the normalization by the product of coordinate boundaries in [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity].

source.place: Proof, Steps 3 and 4: reduction of the Kummer boundary and affine orientations, using the unrestricted supported Cartier map

proof.text:
Step 4 (the diagonal identification). Let $W=X\times_YX$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], $N_\Delta=T_{X/Y}$ is a vector bundle of rank $d$. With section invariants as in [def-pur-section-invariant], the canonical map of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] is the chain
$$\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_A(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\delta_A}C_A(\pi_T,0_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d].$$
The first arrow is the inverse of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], pulled back along $\Delta$, using $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$; Steps 1 and 2 identify its reduction with the same arrow over $B$. The last arrow is $L0_T^*$ of vector-bundle purity, so its reduction is the $B$-arrow by [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] and Step 1. The middle arrow is the normalized map of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. Apply [lem-pur-finite-dnc-normalization-reduction] to $(p_1,\Delta)$: its schemes are separated finite-type, $p_1$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$, and $\Delta$ is a closed section. Its conclusion identifies the reduced middle arrow with $\delta_B$. Composing the three reduced arrows gives exactly $\alpha_{f,B}$, hence $Q\alpha_{f,A}=\alpha_{f,B}$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: explicit diagonal/DNC/vector-bundle chain replacing the invalid general fibrewise-equality argument in Step 1

proof.text:
Step 5 (the square for arbitrary $K$). By [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] its map is
$$\gamma_{f,K}=\theta_{f,K}\circ(1_{Lf^*K}\otimes\alpha_{f,A}^{-1})\circ\tau_{f,K},$$
where $\tau$ is the canonical twist reassociation. Step 1 and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] give $Q\tau_{f,K}=\tau_{f,QK}$. Step 4 gives $Q(\alpha_{f,A}^{-1})=\alpha_{f,B}^{-1}$, since functors preserve inverses. Step 2 gives $Q\theta_{f,K}=\theta_{f,QK}$ after the pullback/tensor/exceptional identifications. Functoriality of $Q$ sends the displayed three-factor composite to the identical three-factor composite for $QK$. These are exactly the two paths around the required square, proving it for every bounded constructible finite-Tor $K$.

source.place: Proof, Steps 2 and 3: paste coefficient comparisons for the three constituents of the purity map

proof.text: Step 6 (trace, composition and base change). The smooth trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace] is $\epsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K})$. By Step 5 and the compact-support comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], its second factor reduces to $Rf_!(\gamma_{f,QK})$; by [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] its first factor reduces to $\epsilon_{f,QK}$. Their composite is therefore $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,QK}$, including $K=A_Y$. In [thm-pur-composition-coherence], the three factors are $Lf^*\gamma_g$ with its twist, $\gamma_f$ evaluated on $Rg^!K$, and $c_{g,f}^{-1}$. Step 5 applies also to $Rg^!K$, which lies in the finite-Tor constructible domain of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; Step 1 identifies its reduction with $Rg_m^!QK$. Hence the first two factors reduce to those for $QK$, and Step 2 does the same for $c_{g,f}^{-1}$. The source identification reduces by twist additivity and pullback associativity. This proves preservation of that composition diagram, rather than merely its commutativity at each level. Finally [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange] explicitly defines the exchange in [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence] as $\gamma_{f',Lv^*K}\circ a\circ(Lu^*\gamma_{f,K})^{-1}$, where $a$ is pullback composition with the twist. Steps 1 and 5 reduce these three factors respectively to $\gamma_{f',Lv^*QK}$, the pullback identification over $B$, and $(Lu^*\gamma_{f,QK})^{-1}$. Thus the right edge, left edge and both horizontal maps of the base-change square are their specified $B$-versions, proving compatibility of the whole square. Step 3 already proved the orientation clause, so all assertions follow.

$$

commutes, the vertical isomorphisms being the finite-reduction

proof.text:
Step 1: the purity map is determined fibrewise, so the comparison may be
made on the geometric fibres. The value of the smooth purity map
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] over a geometric point $\bar y\to Y$
is prescribed by the purity of the geometric fibre $X_{\bar y}$, which
is the affine-space case [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity]
together with the rank-one computation
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. Two natural transformations
between the same pair of exact functors of $K$ that agree on every
geometric fibre agree: the strict henselizations of $Y$ at its
geometric points are pro-etale over $Y$ and jointly surjective, hence
form a pro-etale covering family, and isomorphy of a morphism of
complexes of pro-etale sheaves is local for covering families, clause
(1) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]; it is
therefore enough to compare the two composites of the square fibrewise,
which the compatibilities below do.
Step 2: the reduction compatibilities of the operations. All these
constructions are built from the operations of the six-operations
package, whose finite-reduction compatibilities

$$
(Lf^*K)_m\cong Lf_m^*K_m,\qquad
(Rf^!K)_m\cong Rf_m^!K_m,\qquad
(K(d))_m\cong K_m(d)
$$

are natural in $K$ and in the morphism, by
[def-weil-derived-tensor] and
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] (finite reduction is the derived tensor product along
$A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$; this ring map need not be flat, and the
finite-Tor condition is essential for boundedness). The reduction
functor does land in $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_{E,m})$ with the same Tor interval:
if $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ it has a bounded flat model in
degrees $[a,b]$ by [lem-sf-flat-model], and the reduction of that model
is a bounded flat model of $K_m$ in $[a,b]$ by
[lem-sf-reduction-flat-model]. Compatibility
with pullback and the invertible twist follows from associativity
of derived tensor. For the smooth exceptional inverse image use
the previously constructed tensor formula and its coefficient
compatibility, rather than flat base change. The composition
identifications are those of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (the functoriality of
$R^!$ and of the composition isomorphisms), and by
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed] (the coefficient twists are reduced
coefficient twists). Step 3: the glueing data reduce. The sheaf
axiom gluing used in [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] is a statement
about finite locally constant rank-one sheaves, and the reduction of a
finite locally constant rank-one sheaf is again one; the local
normalizations of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] are the reductions of
the normalizations, the lisse-uniqueness of
[lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness] reduces, and the splitting-principle
descent of one element of an abelian group used in
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] reduces for the same reason
(the Künneth and supported-cohomology groups of
[lem-pur-kunneth-supported] are compatible with the coefficient
reduction, the boundary of the Kummer class reducing to the boundary
of the reduced Kummer class). Hence the vertical isomorphisms of the
square identify $\operatorname{red}_{n,m}(\gamma_{f,K})$ with
$\gamma_{f,\operatorname{red}_{n,m}K}$, which is the commutativity
of the displayed square. Step 4: the remaining statements. The
affine orientations of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] are
constructed from the Kummer boundary, whose reduction is the boundary
of the reduced Kummer class, i.e. the reduction of the orientation;
the smooth trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace] reduces because the
counit of the adjunction reduces (the adjunction itself is compatible
with the finite reduction of the coefficient ring); the composition
and base-change coherence statements are the compatible systems
obtained from Steps 1–3 applied to the constituents of the two
squares.
